item.title: A $2,000 iPhone Gives New Apple CEO John Ternus His Steve Jobs Moment
item.description: When John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as chief executive officer of Apple Inc. at the start of this month, he needed no introduction to the company’s more than 160,000 employees. The same can’t really be said of the public, most of whom will be meeting, and sizing up, Apple’s new top boss for the first time on Wednesday. He’ll begin by making the case for buying an iPhone that costs at least $2,000.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: The Fed’s Three Choices as Warsh’s Honeymoon Ends
item.description: With a week until a key Federal Reserve meeting, President Donald Trump has lobbed his first threat at Kevin Warsh, the new chair he put on the job. “The Fed Board, with its great new leader, must get smart — BE PATRIOTS for a change,” he posted Friday, urging policymakers to cut interest rates even as the market sees better-than-even odds of a hike to counter inflation. Trump added: “High interest rates put the U.S.A. at a very unfair disadvantage, and I won’t allow that to happen!”
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: UK Politics: Andy Burnham’s Signature Devolution Policy May Be His Undoing
item.description: The one thing we know about Britain’s new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, other than that he’s from the north, is that he wants to devolve more power to local government. On everything else he has been vague. Public ownership of utilities? The details are in the post. A closer relationship with the European Union? Fine so long as it doesn’t disturb the results of the Brexit referendum. But the former mayor of Manchester has no choice but to deliver something substantial on devolution, his signature

item.title: Farage's Rule-Breaking Is a Feature of Reform, Not a Bug
item.description: When Nigel Farage returned to the House of Commons after triggering an unnecessary by-election this summer, he marked the occasion with a video filmed from Parliament’s rooftop. The honey-hued stonework of the Palace of Westminster, set against a clear blue sky, created a fabulous social-media backdrop. Unfortunately, for safety and security reasons, filming on Parliament’s roof is strictly forbidden — as anyone who’s worked on the estate knows. The authorities duly reprimanded Farage.

item.title: Heatwaves Are Making Europe's Politicians Look Clueless Again
item.description: For an image of the political madness spawned by the sweltering northern summer of 2026, try this: A UK council in June had to cancel a debate on ending “climate emergency” policies — because of a heatwave alert.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Only the Supreme Court Can End Trump's Mail Ballot Chaos
item.description: Over the holiday weekend, the Trump administration appealed a Friday ruling on mail-in ballots, asking the US Supreme Court to allow it to use the US Postal Service to choke off access to the voting method used by one-third of all Americans. But in many ways, the president has already won the battle by seeding doubt and chaos into the process.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Freight Brokers Need a Safety Net After Supreme Court Ruling
item.description: US freight brokers are still a bit dazed and confused from a bombshell Supreme Court ruling in May that clarified whether these cargo matchmakers should be held liable for truck accidents.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Texas Power Grid Is Being Transformed by Solar Power
item.description: It seems the Trumpian recession in US green energy fails to apply to one of the more Trumpian areas of the country: Texas. Solar power and batteries are taking large bites out of America’s biggest state power grid in the US, and helping to suppress electricity prices in the process.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: The US Military Is Running Out of Weapons. Thank Congress
item.description: “Protecting our nation from those who would do us harm is the first and most important responsibility of government.” That’s from the website of Senator Amy Klobuchar, a Minnesota Democrat. But it could be any lawmaker, or any president, Democrat or Republican. Almost all proclaim it, and by their own standard, almost all are failing — as they have for years, with no end in sight.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: TWG Global Episode Proves Americans' Annuities Deserve Oversight
item.description: Every year, Americans send hundreds of billions of dollars of retirement savings to life insurers in return for annuities that promise a future income. It’s an industry built on trust and prudence.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: MAHA’s Strange Pivot to Its Least-Popular Ideas
item.description: “Bobby Unleashed” is the West Wing’s midterms motto, according to reporting by Politico. But what exactly is Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. being unleashed to do? Because the biggest MAHA policy reforms have run into that familiar Washington foe: old-fashioned bureaucracy. And while many Americans still do want to “Make America Healthy Again,” there are now plenty of other concerns competing for voters’ attention.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey
